response.title: which power station runs an electric cooler for the most days
response.answer:
For running an electric cooler for the most days, the best power station is one with a large battery capacity (Wh), low standby power consumption, and expandable batteries.

The key distinction is what type of electric cooler you have:

12V compressor cooler (Dometic, ICECO, BougeRV, etc.): Very efficient. A large power station can run one for several days or even weeks.

Thermoelectric cooler: Much less efficient. It often draws power continuously and can drain the same battery several times faster.

For a typical 12V compressor cooler averaging 15 watts over a full day, here is the approximate runtime:

For running an electric cooler for the most days, **the best power station is one with a large battery capacity (Wh), low standby power consumption, and expandable batteries.**

The key distinction is what type of electric cooler you have:

- **12V compressor cooler (Dometic, ICECO, BougeRV, etc.):** Very efficient. A large power station can run one for several days or even weeks.

For a typical 12V compressor cooler averaging 15 watts over a full day, here is the approximate runtime:

| Battery capacity | Estimated runtime |
|---|---|
| 1,000 Wh | 2.5 days |
| 2,000 Wh | 5 days |
| 3,600 Wh | 9 days |
| 5,000 Wh | 12.5 days |
| 7,000 Wh | 17.5 days |

These are estimates assuming 90% usable energy, not guaranteed runtimes. Hot weather, frequent opening, and freezing food will reduce them.

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(15)}

    <caption>Compressor coolers may average 10–25W; thermoelectric coolers can consume substantially more.</caption>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row align="center" justify="between">
      <label>Usable battery efficiency</label>
      **{eff}%**
    </row>
    <slider min={65} max={95} step={5} value={eff} onChange={setEff}/>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" padding={3} radius="lg" align="center" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated runtime without recharging</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{days.toFixed(1)} days</title>
    <caption>{(days*24).toFixed(0)} hours</caption>
  </box>
</box>

**One question:** What brand and model is your electric cooler (for example, ICECO VL45, Dometic CFX3 45, or BougeRV 30QT)?

With that, I can compare power stations by **actual expected days of cooling**, rather than battery capacity alone, and identify the most practical choice.
